steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to prepare for creating an Angular component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module paths. Component is needed for the decorator, CommonModule provides basic Angular directives.
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are correctly added at the top of the file, enabling the use of Component decorator and CommonModule.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the necessary Angular modules. This sets up the foundation for creating your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one of the required modules. Make sure to import both Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Set the selector to 'app-root' and template to an empty string for now.
steps.hint: Use the Component import from step 1. The class should be exported and have an empty template.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Define the AppComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator, selector 'app-root', and an empty template.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is exported, has @Component decorator with selector 'app-root' and template ''.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic Angular component structure. This is the foundation for our key press detection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have: 1) @Component decorator, 2) selector 'app-root', 3) template '' (empty string), 4) exported class.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the Component import and define the class with the decorator.

steps.title: Add HostListener import for keyboard event handling
steps.instruction: Import HostListener from '@angular/core' in your existing import statement.
steps.hint: Add HostListener to the import list from '@angular/core' alongside Component and CommonModule.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a module
import { Component, OnInit, HostListener } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Define the AppComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement now includes HostListener, enabling keyboard event handling in the component.
successCriteria: HostListener is imported from '@angular/core' in the import statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported HostListener, which will allow your component to listen to keyboard events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure HostListener is included in the import statement from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: HostListener needs to be imported from '@angular/core' to handle keyboard events. Check the import statement.

steps.title: Create a keyPressed property to track the last pressed key
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add a public property named keyPressed of type string to store the last pressed key. Initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Declare the property with the correct type annotation: keyPressed: string = '';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed property to store keyboard input data.
successCriteria: AppComponent has a public keyPressed property of type string initialized with an empty string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the keyPressed property to track keyboard input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure keyPressed is declared as a public property with type string and initialized with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The keyPressed property is missing or incorrectly declared. It should be a public string property initialized with ''.

steps.title: Define a handleKeyPress method with HostListener decorator
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, create a method named handleKeyPress that takes a KeyboardEvent parameter. Decorate it with @HostListener('window:keydown') to capture keyboard events.
steps.hint: Use the @HostListener decorator imported earlier. The method should update the keyPressed property with the event's key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a properly typed event handler method that responds to keyboard events.
successCriteria: A handleKeyPress method decorated with @HostListener('window:keydown') is defined, taking a KeyboardEvent parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an event handler method with proper typing and decorator.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the method has the @HostListener decorator with 'window:keydown' and accepts a KeyboardEvent parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method is missing or incorrectly defined. Check that it uses @HostListener and has the correct parameter type.

steps.title: Implement the handleKeyPress method to update keyPressed
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, implement the handleKeyPress method to extract the pressed key from the event and assign it to the keyPressed property.
steps.hint: Use the event parameter's 'key' property to get the pressed key string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleKeyPress method will now properly capture which key was pressed and store it in the component's keyPressed property.
successCriteria: The handleKeyPress method extracts event.key and assigns it to this.keyPressed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your handleKeyPress method correctly extracts the pressed key from the event and updates the component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the method, but make sure you're extracting the 'key' property from the event and assigning it to this.keyPressed.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleKeyPress method isn't implemented correctly. It should extract the key from the KeyboardEvent and update the keyPressed property.

steps.title: Add basic template structure with a container div
steps.instruction: In the @Component decorator's template property, add a <div> element that will serve as the container for your key press display.
steps.hint: Look for the empty template string in the @Component decorator and replace it with a <div> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a basic container div element.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator's template property contains a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the container div that will hold your key press display.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a <div> element inside the template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template still appears to be empty. Add a <div> element to the template property.

steps.title: Display the last pressed key in the template
steps.instruction: Update the template to display the value of the keyPressed property using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the component property to the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the last pressed key when you run the app and press any key.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation {{ keyPressed }} to display the property value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully bound the keyPressed property to the template using interpolation. Now the UI will show which key was last pressed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact property name 'keyPressed' inside the interpolation syntax {{ }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template needs to display the keyPressed property value. Use interpolation with double curly braces like {{ keyPressed }}.

steps.title: Add conditional display for when no key has been pressed
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an *ngIf directive to show a default message when keyPressed is empty. Use the existing paragraph that displays the key, and add a fallback message when no key has been pressed yet.
steps.hint: You can use Angular's *ngIf directive with an else clause to conditionally show different content based on whether keyPressed has a value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: conditional rendering with *ngIf

{{ message }}

No message yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now conditionally displays either the last pressed key or a default message when no key has been pressed yet.
successCriteria: The template includes an *ngIf directive that checks if keyPressed is empty and shows a fallback message using an else clause.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to handle the case when no key has been pressed yet.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use *ngIf with an else clause to show the fallback message when keyPressed is empty.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to add an *ngIf directive to conditionally show either the keyPressed value or a default message.

steps.title: Style the key display with basic CSS
steps.instruction: Add a CSS class to the paragraph that displays the last pressed key, then define that class in the component's styles array to make the key display visually distinct.
steps.hint:
Add a class attribute to the

element, then define the corresponding CSS rules in the @Component decorator's styles array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The key display paragraph will have visual styling (like different color, font size, or background) when you press keys.
successCriteria: The paragraph has a CSS class attribute and corresponding CSS rules are defined in the styles array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added visual styling to make the key display stand out. This provides clear visual feedback when users interact with the keyboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both added a class to the paragraph element AND defined the corresponding CSS rules in the styles array of the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling isn't working yet. Remember to add a class attribute to the paragraph element and define the CSS rules for that class in the styles array.
